customManagers.description: Track Go for THIS REPO's line. One repo ships one line, so the cap keeps it on 1.26.x: Go 1.27 arrives as a new repo (see NEXT-LINE-WATCH), never as a bump here.

Watch upstream Go for a NEW LINE. Deliberately uncapped, unlike the go-126 manager: the cap on the shipping line is what keeps this repo on 1.26.x, so something must stay uncapped or a new minor would never be visible here. Bumping this file changes nothing that ships; the PR is the notification that a new repo may be wanted.

packageRules.description: The go-latest watch must never automerge: the shared preset's default is automerge=true, and an un-ruled PR would merge itself when green and nobody would see it. The PR IS the notification that a new Go line exists, so a human has to see it and merge it deliberately -- this is not a version cap (no allowedVersions), just a merge gate.

The 126 line stays on 1.26.x. Not an automerge exception -- automerge is the family default (ship-if-green) and still applies; this only stops Renovate from walking the line onto a Go minor it was never built for.

The BOOTSTRAP Go (actions/setup-go) stays on this repo's line too. Go is self-hosting, so this is the compiler that builds the toolchain we ship -- an ingredient, not CI trivia. Left uncapped it automerged its way onto 1.27 in a repo capped to 1.26.x, silently changing a shipped artifact's inputs with a green build as the only signal, and putting the string '1.27' in a repo that must never build it. A new Go line is a new repo; NEXT-LINE-WATCH is what tells us one exists.
